# Nod

> Nod is a Stellar wallet that lives inside the AI you already use. Apps are turning into conversations and agents, so the wallet sits in the chat: one connector URL in Claude, Goblin, Claude Code or any MCP app, and in ChatGPT as a developer-mode connector. You sign up with a passkey and hold USDC; you never meet XLM, a seed phrase or a trustline. You give each AI app one allowance, say 5 USDC until tomorrow. Inside it, the app pays for APIs over x402 and pays people on its own. Anything past it needs your passkey, every time, for any amount. The allowance is an OpenZeppelin spending-limit policy on your own Stellar account, so the most Nod's service could ever spend for an AI app is the allowance you set, pocket included. Small stuff, it just pays. Big stuff needs your nod.

Read https://trynod.si/SKILL.md and follow it before paying anything on a user's behalf.

Built at HackMeridian 2026 (Lisbon, 25–26 October 2026), Genesis builder track, Stellar Composed thematic track. The full flow runs on Stellar mainnet at trynod.si, in claude.ai, on the founder's own wallet: an x402 purchase settled by OpenZeppelin Channels, a payment inside the allowance, one that needed the nod, a claim link that created a trustline and paid in one transaction, a revoke that removed the rule and swept the pocket.

## Hosts

- https://trynod.si/ is the product on Stellar mainnet: open to anyone, USDC only; fund it from any exchange or wallet through your deposit address, no memo, and it lands in your wallet; or top up from another chain. MCP connector: https://trynod.si/mcp
- https://testnet.trynod.si/ is the judges' sandbox on Stellar testnet. New wallets get 10 testnet USDC; no real money moves. MCP connector: https://testnet.trynod.si/mcp
- https://testnet.trynod.si/sample runs a sample agent through the same tools on Nod's own demo wallet, with a live log and explorer links. No Claude needed.
- The old host hack-meridian-testnet.kristjan-grm11775.workers.dev redirects to testnet.trynod.si.

## Try it on the sandbox

- In Claude: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, URL https://testnet.trynod.si/mcp. In Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http -s user nod https://testnet.trynod.si/mcp`.
- On the page that opens, create a passkey wallet and set Claude's allowance: 5 USDC until tomorrow 12:00 UTC.
- Ask Claude "Buy the market brief" (0.10 USDC over x402, no prompt; 4.90 left), "Send Alice 2 USDC" (paid on its own; 2.90 left), "Pay Bob 5 USDC for dinner" (more than what is left, so it needs your nod: open the link and approve with your passkey; the allowance stays 2.90), the same request again (the same receipt; Bob is paid once), "Send Alice 4 USDC" (needs your nod), "Send Carol 1 USDC" (Carol has never held USDC: after your nod she gets a claim link, and her trustline and the payment land in one transaction). Then revoke Claude under Connections.
- More to try (live on testnet), after revoking: reconnect Claude, create a new wallet on the consent page (10 more testnet USDC) and keep the 5 USDC allowance, then ask "Send 6 USDC to Jan, he isn't on Stellar" (past the allowance: your nod makes a link that is an allowance for Jan alone, exactly 6 USDC for seven days), "Send 1 USDC to Mia; she isn't on Stellar yet, so make her a claim link" (inside the allowance), "Add Dave to my contacts with address GCCZ3V53QHGVWMJJ4AJZJPGCPQVRAWK3B2KAWR6QLTYNHJHEPUJHBIE3, then send him 0.50 USDC" (the first payment to a contact Claude added needs your nod), "Raise my allowance to 6 USDC for two days" (a link your passkey signs).
- Full judge test path with expected results: https://github.com/grmkris/hack-meridian-2026/blob/main/evidence/JUDGE-TEST-PATH.md

## How it works

- Passkey wallet: Face ID or a fingerprint creates an OpenZeppelin smart account (a Stellar contract account). Nod's relayer accounts are the transaction source and pay every network fee, so the owner holds no XLM.
- One allowance per AI app: connecting an app over OAuth 2.1 and setting its allowance with the passkey is one step. Each allowance is a context rule on the account: the app's own Ed25519 key, OpenZeppelin's spending-limit policy (the total the app may spend on its own) and an expiry.
- Past the allowance: the payment is never signed with the app's key. It becomes a link showing the recipient's name and address, the amount and which app asked; the passkey signs that payment on Nod's own page, never in the chat, whatever the amount. Approved payments do not use the allowance.
- Cards and notifications: Nod serves MCP Apps cards (ui://nod/card/v1, ui://nod/home/v1) and ten MCP Events (payment.received, payment.settled, approval.needed, allowance.changed, request.received, request.answered, topup.pending, topup.detected, topup.arrived, topup.expired) by webhook or poll, with 23 MCP tools, on the 2025 MCP protocol and on 2026-07-28, where the nod is a native URL request. Cards and the nod are shown live in Goblin, claude.ai and ChatGPT (developer-mode connector; not listed in ChatGPT's app store, whose policy bars crypto transfers). Events arrive live where the host subscribes, in Goblin and ChatGPT's Work chats; claude.ai and Claude Code do not implement MCP Events, so there the cards poll.
- Paid APIs: x402 sellers are paid through public facilitators (x402.org, OpenZeppelin Channels), never one Nod runs. Hosted facilitators do not take smart-account payers yet, so each AI app's key also owns a small pocket account with sponsored reserves, filled from the wallet under the same policy in 1 USDC steps, which pays with the stock x402 client. Both transactions are on the receipt. Ask twice, pay once.
- Claim link: a recipient with no USDC trustline gets a link. The sender nods once; the recipient accepts with Freighter within 30 minutes (their account needs about 0.5 XLM for the trustline reserve), and a small router calls the USDC contract's trust function (CAP-73) and the transfer in one transaction.
- Revoke: Nod stops signing at once and sweeps the pocket back; one passkey tap removes the allowance from the account.
- Sign up with a passkey and a deposit (live on mainnet and testnet): a wallet can start with nothing onchain and a G… deposit address any exchange can pay. Nod's deposit router binds the address to that one wallet; anyone can sweep what arrives, it can only go to that wallet, and Nod deploys the account when the first USDC lands. Every wallet gets one under Home → Add money; sandbox signups still get 10 testnet USDC.
- Top up from any chain (live on mainnet; 1Click has no testnet): Add money → From another chain, or ask Claude (wallet_topup_quote, wallet_topup_status). NEAR Intents' 1Click swaps what you send from Base, Solana, Ethereum, Arbitrum or Polygon and pays USDC to the wallet's deposit address; Nod sweeps it in. Proof so far: dry-run quotes through Nod's own client against the hosted API, 5 USDC on Base → 4.98 USDC on Stellar in about 50 s (https://github.com/grmkris/hack-meridian-2026/blob/main/evidence/topup/dry-quote-2026-10-25T22-07-19-789Z.json); a funded top-up follows. The two tools were appended after the first 21, which are byte-identical.
- Pay someone who is not on Stellar (live on testnet): Claude makes a claim link for a name; the person opens it, creates a wallet with a passkey (no XLM, no trustline) or signs in, and the USDC lands there. Inside the allowance the link pays from it when claimed.
- A link that is an allowance for one person (live on testnet): past the allowance, the sender's one passkey tap installs a rule for exactly the amount, valid seven days. The link's key is made in the sender's browser and lives only in the link; Nod stores the public key and the rule id. The recipient's browser signs the transfer with that key; Nod relays it and pays the fee. Nothing leaves the sender's wallet until the claim, a second claim is refused, and the sender can take an open link back under Connections → Links. Nod never holds the link key or the funds; a leaked link can take at most the amount, once, before it expires.
- Contacts from the chat (live on testnet): Claude can add, update and remove contacts; the first payment to a contact an AI app added needs the owner's nod, later ones go alone inside the allowance. Claude can ask to change its allowance; that is a link the passkey signs, and the new allowance replaces the old rule.

- 5 USDC to Bob, past the 2.90 left, approved with the passkey (the same request again returned the same receipt): https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/0339b8dd088b46d500de425d0afe8707ff6922186ef70070396323f2d3312e4f
- 1 USDC to Carol, who had no USDC trustline: trustline and payment in one transaction: https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/1fe4e852314ea638ed53ba79acebc60a129b587e0ef80c9b051d434aa01e68c6

- Later (20:53 UTC, after reconnecting): Claude bought Stellar's own x402 demo endpoint https://stellar.org/x402-demo/api/protected/mainnet for 0.01 USDC, a seller Nod does not run, settled through OpenZeppelin Channels to Stellar's pay-to account: https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/3a63573ab65fc557c86737af029bd79b0d382f3ebe78eb5911b3a597f55b596e
- Later (21:44–21:46 UTC): a stranger-style signup with nothing onchain, funded by an ordinary 1 USDC payment with no memo to its deposit address https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/d1c910740917987ba0149edf5be778af702c3f18e83b2bb6d4c1b144658719ec; the deposit router swept it into the wallet https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/7c57d530372b32fe07aac7ea9220380ff52ce54a329518ff838179357329d7af and Nod deployed the account at its planned id 83 s later https://stellar.expert/explorer/public/tx/57b97375c2f1cb8dbfbe122afa9a709c585e536b831b329e6236ef540284796f; the user never held XLM. Record: https://github.com/grmkris/hack-meridian-2026/blob/main/evidence/mainnet/deposit-2026-10-25T21-46Z.md
- Other Stellar x402 sellers checked the same evening: Stellar's own x402 demo endpoint is the one third-party seller we found settling on mainnet today, and we paid it; Nulucre's pubnet price names the testnet USDC contract, so a mainnet payment cannot settle; StellarSight's discovery index holds example entries.
